evals.prompt: Give me a full overview of my network stats
evals.expected_output: Dashboard of global, bandwidth, alerts and summary with tunnel names
expectations: Calls /api/stats/global, /api/stats/bandwidth, /api/stats/alerts and /api/stats/summary
Calls the Stats API with params in the query string and the token in the X-Auth-Token header through stdin, never in the URL
Maps tunnel_token keys to tunnel names via list_tunnels and never prints a tunnel_token
Presents results in a concise table or dashboard

evals.prompt: Show my bandwidth usage for the last hour
evals.expected_output: Peak Mbps per tunnel and in total
expectations: Calls /api/stats/bandwidth with no start (the default is the last hour) or with start/end as RFC3339 UTC in the query string
Does not send an hours or last param to bandwidth
Presents peak_in and peak_out in Mbps per tunnel name and in total, and does not present them as transferred GB
Can report the granularity of the answer

evals.prompt: What's being blocked on my network?
expectations: Calls /api/stats/alerts?last=1d (query string)
Shows block_count and category_counts (for example ads, tracking, malware)
Lists the top blocked domains with tunnel names, not tunnel tokens

evals.prompt: Give me a monthly summary of my network
expectations: Calls /api/stats/summary?days=30
Shows bandwidth.total_peak_in/out (the highest single-tunnel peak) and by_tunnel keyed by tunnel name
Shows the alerts totals by type
Uses list_tunnels to map tunnel tokens to names and never prints the tokens

evals.prompt: Are there any security threats? Show me the last week
expectations: Calls /api/stats/alerts?last=7d, optionally with type=security_event
Groups security events by their value (dangerous_port, port_scan, dns_bypass, doh_bypass)
Highlights concerning patterns or high counts

evals.prompt: How many things were blocked on my iPhone since I connected?
expectations: Calls /api/stats/alerts with last=session AND the iPhone tunnel's tunnel_token (resolved by name in the shell)
Knows that last=session without tunnel_token returns 400
Explains that the session is the app's Live Activity session and zero counts mean no session
Does not print the tunnel_token

evals.prompt: Show me alerts for the last 3 hours
evals.expected_output: Uses start instead of an invalid last value
expectations: Uses start (RFC3339 UTC, three hours ago) instead of a last value, because last accepts only 1m, 1h, 1d/24h, 7d, 30d, session
Writes the time with Z, not +00:00, in the query string
Shows plain-text API errors (such as a 400) to the user as given
